children: Small-cap index falls 5 per cent in a week as foreign outflows and global rate concerns weigh on broader equities

The Nifty Smallcap 100 index fell for a fifth straight session on Wednesday, declining 2 per cent in intraday trade as a broad selloff in equities weighed on smaller companies. The index has fallen 5 per cent over the past week, compared with a 2 per cent decline in the Nifty 50, after having gained 25 per cent over the preceding six months.

The latest decline came amid continued foreign institutional selling and caution ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s monetary policy decision later on Wednesday. Rising US Treasury yields and elevated crude oil prices have also added to pressure on risk assets globally.

Afcons Infrastructure was among the steepest decliners, falling as much as 14 per cent during intraday trading. Pine Labs, Tata Chemicals, Firstsource Solutions, Welspun Corp, Data Patterns (India) and Narayana Hrudayalaya declined between 4 per cent and 6 per cent, according to market data.

Whirlpool of India, Ircon International, Brainbees Solutions and Afcons Infrastructure also touched their respective 52-week lows during the session. The declines came as weakness extended across the broader market following the previous session’s sharp fall in benchmark equities.

The Nifty 50 had fallen 1.19 per cent on Tuesday, while the Sensex declined 1.04 per cent, according to market data. The broader market came under additional pressure as investors assessed the impact of higher commodity prices and bond yields on equities.

Foreign institutional investors remained net sellers in Indian equities for a fifth consecutive session on 15 September, selling shares worth Rs 2,977.86 crore on a net basis. Domestic institutional investors, meanwhile, remained buyers with net purchases of Rs 2,686.05 crore, according to exchange data.

The continued foreign outflows have coincided with a period of heightened global market volatility. Higher US Treasury yields can affect the relative attractiveness of emerging-market assets, while elevated crude prices add to concerns around inflation and corporate costs for oil-importing economies such as India.

Global investors were awaiting the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision on Wednesday, with markets pricing in a 25-basis-point rate increase, according to media reports. The Fed’s accompanying guidance on the path of interest rates is also being closely watched by investors.

The US 10-year Treasury yield briefly moved above 5 per cent before easing to around 4.99 per cent in Asian trading on Wednesday, while Brent crude remained above USD 100 a barrel. The combination of higher yields and elevated oil prices has contributed to a cautious tone across Asian equities.

For Indian equities, the combination of foreign portfolio outflows, global bond yields and commodity prices remains an important factor for near-term market movements. The Nifty Smallcap 100’s five-day decline follows a period of strong gains, with the index still up 25 per cent over the six months preceding the latest week-long correction.
